create.name: Anne Carolyn Klein
create.bio:
Anne Carolyn Klein, also known by her Tibetan name Lama Rigzin Drolma, is a scholar and teacher of Tibetan Buddhism based in Houston, Texas. A professor of religious studies at Rice University, where she once chaired the department, she has spent some four decades studying and practising in the Nyingma Heart Essence tradition of Dzogchen, alongside training in two other Tibetan schools. In 2009 her teacher gave her the title Dorje Lopön, a vajra master. Her books range from studies of Buddhist ways of knowing to a meeting of Buddhist and feminist ideas of the self, along with translations of Dzogchen texts and practice liturgies for English-speaking students.

In 1994 she and her husband, Harvey Aronson (Lama Namgyal Dorje), a psychotherapist and fellow Buddhist teacher, founded Dawn Mountain, a Tibetan Buddhist temple and community centre in Houston. There she leads the Dzogchen Cycles programme, a yearly round of retreats and study for committed students drawing on the lineage of Longchenpa, Jigme Lingpa and Adzom Paylo Rinpoche. Her teaching returns often to the way heart and intellect work together in practice, and she makes room for newcomers too: an online course recorded with Harvey introduces attention, closeness and the four immeasurables. Sunday meditations and many Dawn Mountain events can be joined in person or online.

books.title: Being Human and a Buddha Too: Longchenpa's Seven Trainings for a Sunlit Sky
books.author: Anne Carolyn Klein
books.description: The first volume of her House of Adzom series, built around Longchenpa's seven trainings in the awakened mind, with commentary from Adzom Paylo Rinpoche and practices from Jigme Lingpa. It asks what awakening means for people living ordinary human lives today.

books.title: Meeting the Great Bliss Queen: Buddhists, Feminists, and the Art of the Self
books.author: Anne Carolyn Klein
books.description: A study that sets Buddhist accounts of mind and selfhood beside Western feminist thought, with the Tibetan figure of Yeshe Tsogyal, the Great Bliss Queen, at its centre.

books.title: Knowledge and Liberation: Tibetan Buddhist Epistemology in Support of Transformative Religious Experience
books.author: Anne Carolyn Klein
books.description: A scholarly look at how Tibetan Buddhist thinkers separate conceptual understanding from direct experience, and why that difference matters on the path of practice.

books.title: Heart Essence of the Vast Expanse: A Story of Transmission
books.author: Anne Carolyn Klein
books.description: An English version of Jigme Lingpa's foundational practices written so that it can be chanted, with a shorter form by Adzom Rinpoche and an account of how the lineage was handed on.

books.title: Strand of Jewels: My Teachers' Essential Guidance on Dzogchen
books.author: Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche; translated by Anne Carolyn Klein
books.description: Her annotated translation of the core Dzogchen instructions that Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche gathered from his own teachers, her teacher of several decades.

courses.title: Attention and Connection (online course)
courses.description: A self-paced online course of six video lessons in which Anne Klein and Harvey Aronson pair a short meditation with teaching on attention, love and feeling close to others. It closes with the four immeasurables and suits people starting out on the Buddhist path.

courses.title: Dzogchen Cycles
courses.description: A yearly Dzogchen programme at Dawn Mountain made up of three linked retreats (spring, autumn and Tibetan New Year) with teaching in between, a peer group and a trained mentor. Entry is by application, and single retreats can also be taken on their own.
courses.price: $600 to $800 USD per retreat; full programme fee on application
